case_title: PRA VAT CHANDRA MOHANTY v. THE STATE OF ODISHA
aggravating_circumstances: Beating of a person in the Police Station, which caused fear in the entire society
mitigating_circumstances: Accused are more than 75 years of age
high_court_outcome: Set aside conviction under Section 304 (Part II), upheld conviction under Sections 324/34, 323/34, 471/34
neutral_facts: The accused, who were police officers, beat the victim in the premises of the police station. The victim died the same night. The accused were convicted of causing hurt by dangerous weapons. The trial court found that the description of injuries was minimized in the inquest report by the accused. The High Court upheld the conviction under Section 324 IPC. The accused were willing to compensate the family of the deceased. The victim was beaten so mercilessly that he passed stool, urine, and started bleeding. Eleven injuries were caused on the body of the deceased by the accused. The police officers used wooden lathi and batton as weapons. The evidence of the informant, who was also the eye-witness, was believed by the trial court and the High Court. The accused were more than 75 years of age at the time of the sentence.
